conflicts.quote: During the 10-minute combined soak at REST concurrency 16 and 32 held streams, REST p95 stays at or below 1,000 ms, with zero unexpected REST errors and zero unexpected stream disconnects.
conflicts.why: My R1 makes a 60-second mixed soak mandatory in the normal gate and moves longer execution to an optional 15-minute profile; that cannot satisfy a requirement that the normal verification path itself include this 10-minute scenario.
conflicts.proposal: Have the human choose the gate-cost policy; the closest implementation to PM's position is to make the 10-minute combined soak mandatory, retain any three-minute profile only as a supplementary developer check, and keep both on one manifest/evaluator/report implementation.

conflicts.quote: After warm-up, 200 fixture-backed REST requests at concurrency 16 produce p95 latency at or below 250 ms, no observation above 1,000 ms, and zero unexpected errors.
conflicts.why: My R1 specifies 100 serial measured cache hits, so it exercises neither PM's request count nor its concurrency and cannot be treated as evidence for this acceptance criterion.
conflicts.proposal: Use the PM workload as the closed warm scenario—200 measured requests at concurrency 16 after discarded warm-ups—and preserve the architect's cache-state precondition and immutable observation/evaluator split.

conflicts.quote: Under 320 fixture-backed REST requests at concurrency 32, p95 latency is at or below 1,500 ms, no observation exceeds 5,000 ms, and no unexpected error occurs.
conflicts.why: My R1 proposes two 32-request parallel phases and a 3,000 ms p95 ceiling; the count and threshold define a materially different workload and verdict.
conflicts.proposal: Make PM's 320-request/concurrency-32 workload and thresholds the required parallel scenario; retain the single-cold-identity coalescing burst only as a separately named additional scenario if its gate cost is accepted.

conflicts.quote: macOS support, hosted-runner comparison, 30-minute and overnight endurance profiles, multi-replica exercises, and production-telemetry correlation require separate approval and evidence.
conflicts.why: My R1 requires a macOS resource adapter in v1, while PM explicitly future-dates macOS support; both scopes cannot govern the same required-observation manifest.
conflicts.proposal: Limit v1 required adapters and conformance evidence to Windows 11 and Linux x64, while keeping the sampler port extensible so macOS can be added only after separate approval.

conflicts.quote: When the service attempts any forbidden external connection during a scenario, that scenario and the overall run fail even if all latency and error thresholds otherwise pass.
conflicts.why: My typed fixture assembler, credential stripping, loopback target validation, and live-provider audit guard close the known market-data path, but they do not by themselves observe an arbitrary direct socket introduced later by another dependency on both Windows and Linux; the universal claim currently lacks a named portable enforcement mechanism.
conflicts.proposal: Either narrow the claim to the complete source-verified outbound connector graph and inject a deny-all connector with a poison test, or explicitly add platform sandbox/firewall adapters that deny and audit every non-loopback child-process connection; planning must source-verify which mechanism is feasible before the universal criterion stands.

conflicts.quote: Thirty seconds after all generated traffic drains, no harness-owned request or stream remains active; handles/descriptors and runtime tasks are each no more than 2 above baseline; and resident memory is no more than 64 MiB above baseline.
conflicts.why: My R1 evaluates a 10-second grace, exact subscriber/task return to baseline, and a memory ceiling of the larger of 16 MiB or 10 percent; the observation time and pass thresholds are different and cannot both be the single versioned recovery policy.
conflicts.proposal: Have the human select one recovery policy; the closest synthesis to PM is a 30-second required checkpoint with PM's ceilings, while retaining exact harness-owned subscriber/request accounting as an additional leak invariant when the lifecycle probe can measure it without changing runtime semantics.

conflicts.quote: All are `test` because each can silently regress while the existing product still looks normal; no separate UX test matrix is proposed.
conflicts.why: PM's final criteria classify the bounded-claim guidance and trader-visible no-change criterion as review, so UX's all-test disposition contradicts the acceptance owner and would leave the verification plan with two authorities.
conflicts.proposal: Split the evidence: automated tests and structural empty-diff/route guards cover machine-observable invariants, while PM's review rows remain for the operator-facing claim boundary and before/after trader-visible equivalence.

conflicts.quote: I assume PM accepts a mandatory local profile capped at three minutes plus an optional 15-minute profile; if PM requires the full soak on every normal verification, the gate-cost design and scenario counts must change.
conflicts.why: The PM position requires the 10-minute combined soak in the normal local verification path and sets 15 minutes as the total target; replacing that with a one-minute normal soak and making 15 minutes optional materially weakens the release evidence and changes scope.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the 10-minute combined soak mandatory within the 15-minute total target unless the architect demonstrates that this is infeasible, then present the human with an explicit duration-versus-gate-cost decision rather than silently shortening the scenario.

conflicts.quote: Linux, macOS, and Windows adapters are required; an unavailable adapter is a failed required observation, never a skipped check.
conflicts.why: The PM scope supports Windows 11 and Linux x64 in v1 and explicitly future-dates macOS; making macOS required expands the approved platform scope and could block the feature on work not selected for this release.
conflicts.proposal: Require complete observations and fail unavailable measurements on Windows 11 and Linux x64, while leaving macOS support for the separately approved future scope.

conflicts.quote: REST warm: prime one representative single-ticker request, discard five warm-ups, then measure 100 serial cache-hit requests.
conflicts.why: The PM position defines 200 measured warm requests at concurrency 16; 100 serial requests do not exercise or evidence the selected warm-load guardrail.
conflicts.proposal: Use the PM workload of 200 measured warm requests at concurrency 16, retaining bounded warm-up observations only as setup rather than as a replacement workload.

conflicts.quote: REST parallel: launch 32 clients simultaneously against one cold identity to exercise request coalescing, then 32 clients across eight warm identities to exercise shared read capacity.
conflicts.why: The PM position requires 320 requests at concurrency 32; the proposed two groups of 32 requests change the amount and composition of evidence without an approved product tradeoff.
conflicts.proposal: Retain 320 total requests at concurrency 32 and let architecture distribute those requests across representative identities only if the resulting scenario still measures the selected parallel guardrail.

conflicts.quote: SSE churn: run ten connect/hold/disconnect waves at one quarter of configured capacity, with all clients closing from both orderly and abrupt sides.
conflicts.why: The PM position requires ten full waves of 32 clients; quarter-capacity waves reduce the selected recovery pressure, while adding abrupt closes changes the scenario beyond the approved clean-disconnect requirement.
conflicts.proposal: Keep ten full 32-client connect/disconnect waves as the required scenario; treat abrupt-close coverage as additive only if it does not replace or make the required full-capacity clean-close evidence infeasible.

conflicts.quote: Warm REST must have zero unexpected errors, p95 at or below 250 ms, and p99 at or below 500 ms.
conflicts.why: The selected PM guardrail is p95 at or below 250 ms with no individual observation above 1,000 ms; substituting a p99 ceiling changes both the measured statistic and the breach boundary.
conflicts.proposal: Retain the p95 and per-observation maximum selected by PM; record p99 as supplemental evidence only unless the human explicitly adds it as a blocking guardrail.

conflicts.quote: Cold REST must have zero unexpected errors and p95 at or below 2 seconds.
conflicts.why: The PM position selects cold p95 at or below 3,000 ms and no observation above 5,000 ms; a 2-second p95 omits the maximum and makes the blocking threshold materially stricter without a product ruling.
conflicts.proposal: Use the selected 3,000 ms p95 and 5,000 ms per-observation maximum until measured implementation evidence is presented for an explicit human threshold revision.

conflicts.quote: Both parallel phases must complete every request, have zero unexpected errors, p95 at or below 3 seconds, and finish within 5 seconds wall time.
conflicts.why: The PM position selects a 1,500 ms parallel p95 and a 5,000 ms per-observation maximum; the architect instead doubles the p95 ceiling and introduces a different whole-phase limit.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the 1,500 ms p95 and 5,000 ms per-observation maximum as blocking guardrails, with whole-phase duration recorded as supplemental evidence unless the human changes the threshold set.

conflicts.quote: Accepted SSE connects must have p95 at or below 500 ms; the over-cap refusal must arrive within 500 ms; accepted streams must not disconnect unexpectedly.
conflicts.why: Connection latency and disconnect behavior align, but the PM position selects a 1,000 ms refusal ceiling; tightening refusal to 500 ms is an unapproved change to the blocking threshold.
conflicts.proposal: Retain the 1,000 ms blocking refusal ceiling and optionally report the 500 ms result as non-blocking evidence until the human explicitly revises the guardrail.

conflicts.quote: Quiescent resident memory, defined as the median of the last three samples, may be at most baseline plus the larger of 16 MiB or 10 percent, and three successive post-wave quiet samples may not rise by more than 4 MiB total.
conflicts.why: The PM position selects memory ceilings of 128 MiB above baseline during soak and 64 MiB above baseline 30 seconds after drain; the architect proposes different sampling semantics and much tighter ceilings, so the same observation could receive opposite verdicts.
conflicts.proposal: Use the PM soak and 30-second recovery ceilings for the blocking verdict; retain median and slope observations as diagnostics unless the human explicitly chooses the architect's stricter policy.

conflicts.quote: All are `test` because each can silently regress while the existing product still looks normal; no separate UX test matrix is proposed.
conflicts.why: A blanket automated-test designation conflicts with risk-based verification: machine report, isolation, threshold, and recovery behavior can regress silently and need tests, while the intentional absence of new trader-facing controls, copy, and workflows is directly observable and is appropriately verified by review.
conflicts.proposal: Keep automated verification for silent harness and isolation regressions, and keep review for the trader-visible no-change criterion; a structural source-diff guard may supplement but should not replace that review.

conflicts.quote: I assume UX/Tech Writer owns the exact CLI command names, report member names, diagnostic wording, and operator remediation text; if those are not supplied, the synthesizer must define them without altering the technical report contents described here.
conflicts.why: UX explicitly places final machine-report field names outside its lane, while command and member names are technical contract concerns; leaving ownership ambiguous risks either an invented UI-style contract or missing executable/report vocabulary.
conflicts.proposal: Have the synthesizer bind technical command and report-member names from the architecture shape, while UX owns claim-safe operator wording and diagnostic comprehensibility.

conflicts.quote: A 10-minute combined soak at REST concurrency 16 with 32 held stream clients.
conflicts.why: This mandatory normal-path soak cannot coexist with the architect's requirement that the complete normal profile finish within three minutes and use a 60-second mandatory short soak, while treating a longer profile as separately selectable.
conflicts.proposal: Ask the human to choose one binding normal-gate duration and soak duration, then retain any longer run as a clearly named optional profile rather than blending the two positions.

conflicts.quote: Linux, macOS, and Windows adapters are required; an unavailable adapter is a failed required observation, never a skipped check.
conflicts.why: PM places only Windows 11 and Linux x64 in v1 and explicitly future-dates macOS, so this sentence expands supported-platform scope beyond the product position.
conflicts.proposal: Ask the human to decide whether macOS is a v1 supported platform or a future-dated adapter; whichever scope is chosen must make unsupported required measurements fail honestly on supported platforms.

conflicts.quote: REST warm: prime one representative single-ticker request, discard five warm-ups, then measure 100 serial cache-hit requests.
conflicts.why: PM requires 200 warm requests at concurrency 16, so the positions define different workloads and would produce non-comparable evidence under the same 'warm' label.
conflicts.proposal: Have the human select one v1 warm workload, or explicitly name serial-warm and concurrent-warm as separate required scenarios with independent thresholds and report rows.

conflicts.quote: Cold REST must have zero unexpected errors and p95 at or below 2 seconds.
conflicts.why: PM sets cold p95 at 3,000 ms and adds a 5,000 ms per-observation ceiling; a single cold verdict cannot honestly claim conformance to both threshold policies without declaring which policy is binding.
conflicts.proposal: Ask the human to choose the canonical cold p95 and maximum-observation guardrails; report the selected thresholds beside the measurements rather than silently applying the stricter value.

conflicts.quote: REST parallel: launch 32 clients simultaneously against one cold identity to exercise request coalescing, then 32 clients across eight warm identities to exercise shared read capacity.
conflicts.why: PM instead specifies 320 requests at concurrency 32 under one parallel criterion, with a 1,500 ms p95; the workload identity, request count, cache condition, and threshold are not the same claim.
conflicts.proposal: Ask the human whether v1 needs both coalesced-cold and shared-warm parallel scenarios or one 320-request scenario, then give every retained scenario its own unambiguous name and threshold row.

conflicts.quote: Accepted SSE connects must have p95 at or below 500 ms; the over-cap refusal must arrive within 500 ms; accepted streams must not disconnect unexpectedly.
conflicts.why: PM permits the over-cap refusal to take up to 1,000 ms, so the same refusal observation would pass one position and fail the other.
conflicts.proposal: Ask the human to choose the refusal-latency ceiling and encode that one value in the versioned threshold policy and report.

conflicts.quote: Quiescent resident memory, defined as the median of the last three samples, may be at most baseline plus the larger of 16 MiB or 10 percent, and three successive post-wave quiet samples may not rise by more than 4 MiB total.
conflicts.why: PM defines different soak and recovery memory ceilings of baseline plus 128 MiB and 64 MiB, with recovery observed after 30 seconds; these policies can return different verdicts and use different observation bases.
conflicts.proposal: Ask the human to choose one canonical soak/recovery memory policy, while architecture retains exact subscriber, task, and descriptor recovery as separate evidence rather than using memory alone as a leak claim.

conflicts.quote: I assume UX/Tech Writer owns the exact CLI command names, report member names, diagnostic wording, and operator remediation text; if those are not supplied, the synthesizer must define them without altering the technical report contents described here.
conflicts.why: This assigns machine interface and command naming to the UX lane even though there is no user-facing surface and the UX position explicitly limits itself to claim integrity; final report members and CLI names are technical contract decisions, while UX can review diagnostic and remediation wording.
conflicts.proposal: Architecture should own stable command and report-schema names; UX should own the exact human-readable diagnostics, remediation language, units, and bounded-claim wording without changing machine semantics.

conflicts.quote: A reviewer exercising the trader application before and after this feature observes no new or changed trader-facing control, copy, status, workflow, score, recommendation, or stream behavior.
conflicts.why: Marking this negative-space invariant as review-only leaves a silent UI, payload, scoring, recommendation, or SSE regression unguarded; the verification rule assigns silently regressing invariants to automated tests.
conflicts.proposal: Split AC-21 so visible unchanged trader presentation receives review where useful, while zero dashboard/client-contract diff and unchanged scoring, recommendation, and stream invariants are verified by automated tests.

asks.ask: PM: Are the 10-minute soak, 200-request warm load, 320-request parallel load, and stated resource ceilings binding normal-gate scope, or may a shorter mandatory profile plus an optional extended profile satisfy the product goal?
PM: Should v1 support only Windows 11 and Linux x64, with macOS merely an extension seam, as your future-dated scope states?
UX: What exact operator-facing guidance must accompany the machine report to satisfy the local-baseline-not-production-capacity claim without creating any trader-facing surface?

Architect: can the required 10-minute combined load, 30-second recovery observation, report emission, and setup complete inside the 15-minute total target on both Windows 11 and Linux x64; if not, which measured phase is the feasibility constraint?

Architect: can Windows 11 and Linux x64 provide comparable required observations for resident memory, handles or descriptors, runtime tasks, and active harness-owned requests or streams without treating an unsupported sample as passing?

UX: what operator-facing wording should identify an expected cap refusal and expected fixture not-found outcome without making either read as an unexpected service failure or as successful data delivery?
Architect: which source-read seam can distinguish orderly client closure, abrupt client loss, accepted-stream recovery, and cap refusal without adding a trader or operator HTTP route?
Architect: can the fixture-only child assembly make every non-loopback connection structurally unreachable on both Windows 11 and Linux x64, and what observation proves the guard is non-vacuous?
PM: does 'every accepted client closes cleanly' describe service-side resource recovery after both orderly and abrupt client endings, or does it exclude the architect's abrupt-close churn cases?
